reason: The passage (Genesis 12:1-8) contains explicit divine blessings toward Abraham: God promises to make him a great nation (וְאֶעֶשְׂךָ לְגוֹי גָּדוֹל), to bless him (וַאֲבָרֶכְךָ), to make his name great (וַאֲגַדְּלָה שְׁמֶךָ), and to bless his descendants such that 'all families of the earth shall be blessed in you' (וְנִבְרְכוּ בְךָ כֹּל מִשְׁפְּחֹת הָאֲדָמָה). These unconditional and expansive blessings directed toward Abraham and his future offspring—who would become the Hebrew people—demonstrate Yahweh's clear intention that they prosper and thrive.
